query: What review signals predict negative Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: defect_or_failure
per_column.rationale: Presence of a described product defect is an observable content feature that lies outside the satisfaction label and plausibly drives negative satisfaction without deterministically defining it.

per_column.name: strong_negative_language
per_column.rationale: Emphatic/casual negative language is essentially a restatement of expressed dissatisfaction; it is a direct manifestation of the sentiment/label rather than an independent antecedent signal, so it approaches leakage of label_pos.

per_column.name: regret_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Categories like 'waste_of_money', 'would_not_recommend', and 'regret_or_remorse' are expressions of dissatisfaction itself, effectively restating the negative label rather than predicting it from an external factor.

per_column.name: unmet_expectation
per_column.rationale: Being 'not_as_described' or 'false_advertising' references a concrete product/listing attribute mismatch that is distinguishable from the satisfaction judgment and plausibly causes it, offering some predictive signal.

per_column.name: value_concern
per_column.rationale: 'not_worth_it', 'poor_value', 'overpriced' are evaluative dissatisfaction statements that largely coincide with a negative label rather than serving as an independent predictor of it.

judge.rationale: Most added columns encode expressed dissatisfaction (strong negative language, regret, value complaints), which restate or leak the satisfaction label rather than providing external predictive features; a model using them would largely be reading the outcome off its own manifestation. Only defect_or_failure and unmet_expectation reference concrete, outcome-external product/listing conditions that plausibly cause dissatisfaction and offer legitimate predictive leverage. As a set, genuine predictive value beyond the raw text is limited.
